system_description.narrative_title: Blue wave, AI reckoning, and a fractured security-energy order
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is being reconfigured by a US political shock — a Democratic midterm sweep — that is immediately reshaping domestic policy leverage, markets and the politics of technology, while persistent kinetic and hybrid conflicts (Iran-related strikes, Russia’s attacks on Ukraine) keep energy and security risks elevated. Financial and monetary strains — rising inflation in Europe and higher rates globally — interact with an abrupt rethink of the AI/data‑centre buildout, creating simultaneous market and investment stress. At the same time China is consolidating control over critical minerals and technological levers, and cyber/crypto shocks expose vulnerabilities in global finance and logistics, so geopolitical, economic and technological feedbacks are accelerating system-wide volatility.
system_description.scope: Nation-states and alliances (US, China, Russia, EU, Middle East states, regional powers), global financial markets and sovereign debt, technology and AI industry (data centres, chips, cloud), critical commodity and energy markets, active conflict theaters (Ukraine, Iran-related maritime/strikes), cyber and crypto ecosystems, international institutions and trade regimes — plus the domestic politics that drive foreign policy and regulatory choices.
system_description.super_system: The planetary political-economic-technical system: a globalized capitalist order shaped by transnational markets, digital infrastructure, and ecological/energy constraints.
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial and monetary subsystem (markets, central banks, sovereign debt)
Digital-tech and AI infrastructure subsystem (data centres, chip supply chains, cloud providers)
Middle East security–energy subsystem (Iran, Gulf shipping, oil markets, regional proxies)
Eurasian conflict subsystem (Russia–Ukraine war and European security architecture)

variables.name: U.S. political realignment
variables.description: A dramatic shift in U.S. domestic balance of power as Democrats seized control of Congress, constraining the Trump political project and reshaping the policymaking landscape at home and in U.S. global posture.

variables.name: Iran-Gulf escalation
variables.description: An ongoing cycle of strikes, proxy actions and diplomacy involving Iran, the United States, Israel and Gulf states that is oscillating between military confrontation and mediated talks, raising regional security tensions.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war
variables.description: A sustained high-intensity war in which Russia conducts large-scale attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure while Ukraine and Western partners adjust military aid and pursue intermittent diplomatic avenues.

variables.name: AI build‑out and market correction
variables.description: A global surge in AI infrastructure spending and data‑centre expansion that has produced asset froth, resource and cybersecurity strains and sparked growing political and regulatory backlash as markets reassess valuations.

variables.name: U.S.–China tech and chip rivalry
variables.description: A strategic competition between the United States and China over semiconductors, advanced-technology supply chains and financial/regulatory levers, driven by export controls, investment curbs and national-security concerns.
